Architecture specific mechanics of return address hijack, liveness checks, out of line preparation, and trap detection.
Out of line area and instruction slot allocation, lifetime, and failure handling.
Return consumer identity allocation and cookie contract between entry and return handlers.
Timer cancellation and rearm conditions beyond teardown and successful push.

findings.text: Per task probe teardown detaches the container from its owner and synchronously stops the return scan timer, then drains the pending chain before draining the spare pool, freeing every element and finally the container, warning if single step or out of line state remains active.

Fork handling duplicates the pending return stack when the parent has entries and the address space is new or the clone is a virtual fork, then arranges deferred work to recreate the out of line area in the child, warning on duplication or area failures.

Signal suppression reports whether a probe is mid single step, records denial while clearing the pending flag when signals await, and escalates to a trapped step with resume notification when a fatal signal or trapped out of line execution appears.

System call probe entry resolves the breakpoint address under trace protection, ensures per task state exists, honors architecture ignore policy, then runs the consumer chain without entering single step.

Return trampoline entry walks pending elements chain by chain, checks liveness of each following chain, restores the saved original address, pops each completed element while invoking matching return handlers, and forces an illegal signal when task state or pending elements are missing.
Resume notification clears the probe flag and either finishes an interrupted single step when a probe stays active or treats the resume as a fresh breakpoint hit.

Pre step notification requests probe resume when the address space carries probes or return entries exist, while post step notification acknowledges an active single step and likewise requests resume handling.
Early initialization prepares the mapping hash locks and registers a high priority exception notifier ordered after kernel probes and debugger handling.

Jump label service offers paired lock and unlock around a global mutex plus a table sorting helper that orders a range by key and then by code, using a relative aware exchange on supporting architectures.

Pending return elements form a singly linked stack with a depth count increased on push and decreased on pop, newest at the head, published with ordered assignment, with the scan timer rearmed on every successful push.

Released elements may enter a spare pool, so teardown empties the pending chain before the pool, while allocation prefers the pool before fresh storage and reports a distinguished empty marker on failure.

Duplication copies every pending element in order with linkage and depth preserved, installing either a stably referenced probe or an empty reference while retaining the full chain for correct nesting in the child.

When the hijacked address already equals the trampoline address the new element is marked chained and inherits the saved original address from the existing head, preserving the first caller address across tail calls.
Before pushing, the invalidated prefix is discarded as judged by an architecture liveness predicate whose context separates chained call from plain call and checked return.

Breakpoint handling walks consumers under trace protection, tracks whether any existed and whether all asked removal, gathers return consumers only for entries with return handling that are not ignored, and prepares at most one return element.
Removal driven by handlers is rechecked under the registration lock in read mode before deactivation, guarding against concurrent registration changes.

Breakpoint resolution tries a speculative lock free lookup first, then under read lock validates mapping and offset, separates absent probes from genuine traps, and lazily clears the address space probe flag when a recalculation was requested and none remains.

Timer expiry holds fast sleepable read protection for probe lifetime plus read copy update protection for element lifetime while advancing a sequence counter around expiration of all pending elements, relying on a single writer.
Duplication holds fast sleepable read protection across the whole copy so expiration can safely attempt stable acquisition of each referenced probe.
Preparation acquires a fast sleepable lease that survives return to user space and may be released later by timer expiry or duplication rather than by the preparing context.

Breakpoint and return paths hold trace read protection while walking consumer lists, with the slow lookup path additionally holding the memory map read lock while inspecting mappings and trap contents.
Jump label mutation is serialized by a dedicated global mutex reached only through paired lock and unlock helpers.
Probe deactivation after handler driven removal executes under the probe registration semaphore in read mode.

Per task probe container tracks active probe plus out of line addresses plus stepping state plus signal denial plus return head plus spare pool plus depth plus sequence counter plus timer plus deferred fork work plus current architecture reference.

Return element stores onward linkage plus probed address plus user stack value plus saved original address plus chained marker plus consumer count plus inline first consumer plus overflow array plus lifetime handle.
Jump table element carries code plus target plus key as relative offsets on supporting architectures, so exchange adjusts each field by the distance between slots rather than plain copying.

Stepping moves from stepping to acknowledged on post notification or to trapped on fatal signals or trapped execution, then completion returns to running while releasing the probe reference plus out of line slot and restoring deferred signals.

Breakpoint flow separates trampoline hits for return handling from ordinary hits, restarts when no probe matches a nontrap location, skips stepping when architecture ignores or emulates, otherwise parks the probe active for completion on resume.

Probe lifetime handle starts leased at preparation, may expire under timer or duplication, becomes stable in the child, and is consumed then finalized once during trampoline unwinding, with a path that skips further cleanup when already finalized.
Exceeding the maximum nesting depth discards the new return element with a rate limited notice identifying the process, leaving earlier entries unchanged.
A chained return with an empty pending stack is treated as impossible and likely user interference, warning and discarding the new element.

Unmatched traps force a trap signal, missing task state or missing pending entries at trampoline entry force an illegal signal, and single step post failure likewise forces an illegal signal after cleanup.

Speculative lookup discards results when the memory map sequence changes after dereference, while trap inspection warns and fails on misalignment and falls back to pinned page copying when direct user access fails.
Return scan period is one tenth of a second, expressed as the tick rate divided by ten.
Uprobe exception notifier priority is one below the maximum integer, placing it after kernel probes and debugger handling.
